dedupe_keys.name: ctu nettest open data crowdsourced internet speed and latency measurements czechia

description: ČTÚ-NetTest is the Czech Telecommunication Office's tool for measuring the quality of internet access actually achieved by users, recording download and upload speed and response time (ping) for fixed and mobile connections, in a browser or mobile app. ČTÚ publishes the measurements as open data in a single ZIP file of all data, first released for the 2022 public administration hackathon, with a data specification page describing the fields published. Measurements typically carry the time, network type, operator, device information and an approximate location, which allows maps of achieved speeds. Coverage: Czechia, wherever users run tests. Format and access: ZIP archive of all data and a data specification on the NetTest site, free under ČTÚ open data terms allowing reuse with attribution. Caveats: crowdsourced tests are biased toward users who choose to test and toward problem connections; the catalogue entry was last modified in May 2026 and update frequency is not stated. Simulation uses: evidence of achieved speeds and latencies by area and operator, and baselines for detecting degradation during outages or disasters. Related records: RTR-NetTest in Austria is the tool NetTest derives from, and the ČTÚ mobile measurement and broadband coverage records give regulator-measured and infrastructure views.
